newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian silver ends down, gold steady in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian silver ends down, gold steady in dull trade.

text.p: Silver (.999) closed 55 rupees lower at 6,840 rupees per kg after making a feeble attempt at recovery in the absence of consumer and industrial demand. Silver opened at 6.830 rupees per kg.
Gold was steady at 4,680 rupees per 10 grammes in dull trade. The price of gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) was unchanged at 54,800 rupees per piece.
Dealers said bullion trade was passing through the lean months of June and July after the conclusion of the wedding season in May.
"There's no investor around. Money market is very tight," said a leading jeweller.
He said most families spend money in the summer months of May and June on travel and holidays, children's education and such other annual needs.
Dealers said they expected demand for gold to pick up only after August or September when there would be cash with farmers. (Conversion $1=35.78 rupees)
